Prio Optics leverages proprietary processes to manufacture multilayer optical interference coatings under ambient conditions, eliminating the need for traditional vacuum-based deposition methods. This approach enables cost-effective, scalable, and customizable production of optical coatings on a variety of substrates, including flexible and large-area formats. 
Prio Optics offers a broad portfolio of optical coatings, such as anti-reflection coatings, dichroic coatings, and long-pass filter coatings, catering to applications in smartphone cameras, displays, building window and photovoltaics. 
Prio Optics' inkjet-printed coatings are characterized by higher throughput at lower costs, fast production, low material waste, and minimal environmental impact, aligning with sustainable manufacturing practices.

AHEAD Institute for Societal Advancement Ltd is a Maltese entity specialising in EO downstream services and geospatial R&D for climate and environmental applications. We transform Copernicus and complementary datasets into operational products and services, including high-resolution mapping, change detection, risk indicators, and scenario-based assessments to support adaptation planning and emergency preparedness.
Our technical strengths cover remote sensing, GIS, spatial analytics, AI-enabled decision support, and the development of digital-twin-style modelling environments that integrate terrain, land use, exposure and climate inputs. We deliver stakeholder-ready outputs through interactive web tools, technical reporting, and workflows designed for transparency, reproducibility and integration into existing geospatial infrastructures.
AHEAD’s work targets measurable outcomes: improved situational awareness, better prioritisation of interventions, and scalable methods that can be replicated across small island and coastal contexts relevant to ESA and European resilience objectives.

Nokia’s differentiation includes industry leadership in vertically integrated solutions that include in-house developed photonic integrated circuit (PIC) and application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) chips and unique software solutions packaged together to deliver networks that offer ultra-high performance, yet remain easy to deploy, use and operate.

Coriant R&D GmbH has a significant presence and a proven record of accomplishment in numerous European projects with service providers, component suppliers, universities and research institutes, namely under the EU Seventh Framework Programme (FP7) and Horizon 2020 (H2020). entityDescription: Deplotic is an innovative startup with a mission to enhance the sustainability of space operations by prolonging the operational lifespan of satellites through advanced robotic solutions. Deplotic was founded by a team of researchers from the Politecnico di Torino, who have been working for years on robotics for space applications. Deplotic is developing IDRA, an inflatable and deployable robotic arm. By integrating advanced inflatable technology with modular electric actuation, IDRA offers a solution for space logistics and in-orbit servicing (IOS) operations—enabling satellite operators and service providers to significantly reduce costs, complexity, and integration time associated with traditional robotic systems. Thanks to its inflatable structure, IDRA achieves an unprecedented workspace—up to 64 times larger than conventional manipulators with the same stowed volume—while remaining lightweight, compact, and customizable. Its modular design allows rapid adaptation to specific mission requirements, with adjustable link lengths, degrees of freedom, and tool configurations. IDRA is engineered to support a wide range of tasks, including inspection, repair, refueling, upgrading, satellite relocation, and debris removal, both in-orbit and on planetary surfaces. Unlike traditional manipulators, IDRA can be stowed compactly and deployed on demand, making it ideal for spacecraft with tight volume constraints. Moreover, it enables to perform self-maintenance operations—reaching any part of the host satellite—providing unprecedented autonomy and cost-effectiveness for medium-to-large-sized space assets.

entityDescription:
Calnex NE-ONE Network Emulators enable the easy creation of Software Defined SATCOM Test Networks.
Satellite networks represent a big challenge for applications that are being developed to run on them, or deployed having been built for other network types. This is due to their relatively High Latency, with Jitter, Bit Error and Loss all playing a part.
Any application which can be regarded as SATCOM-Ready needs to be thoroughly tested in a wide range of satellite conditions.
The issue is that obtaining a real and representative SATCOMS network to test over is a challenge, and the costs of doing this are frequently prohibitive.
NE-ONE Software Defined Test Networks (powered by Calnex NE-ONE's hardware and virtual Network Emulators) allow the creation of an end-to-end network which behaves just like a SATCOM network, allowing easy testing of the applications. Unlike real SATCOM networks, it is relatively inexpensive and allows full controllability and repeatability of different Satellite Network Conditions and Types.
NE-ONE Software Defined Test Networks are trusted and relied upon by enterprises, governments and military organisations around the world.

To meet the evolving demands of space photovoltaic applications, we have developed two innovative, technology-agnostic solutions compatible with all major PV platforms, including GaAs, silicon, and perovskite technologies :
1. Cover Glass Booster The Cover Glass Booster is designed to significantly enhance the performance and durability of space PV solar cells and panels, delivering several percentage points of improvement in conversion efficiency while extending operational lifetime. Initially developed for triple-junction PV systems, this solution offers broad compatibility and can be readily adapted to virtually any PV cell or panel architecture. 
2. High-Performance, Long-Longevity UV Filter
As the space sector increasingly explores cost-effective silicon and perovskite PV technologies, resistance to ultraviolet-induced degradation has become a decisive factor for long-term mission success. Our advanced UV filter effectively mitigates degradation caused by UVC, UVB, and UVA radiation, preserving photovoltaic performance and reliability over the entire operational lifespan of the cell or panel.
